L589@P19: The City seeks to house people who are unhoused. The primary driver of homelessness
L590@P19: is a lack of affordable housing, yet there are also tools and strategies that can help guide
L591@P19: some unsheltered people into safer conditions and housing. Measure P has expanded
L592@P19: those tools and strategies.
L593@P19: The City addresses unsheltered homelessness and encampments both by coordinating
L594@P19: services and shelter for those on the street as well as ensuring safe, clean, and accessible
L595@P19: public spaces for all. This interdepartmental work, led by the Homeless Response Team
L596@P19: in Neighborhood Services, is a direct result of an allocation of Measure P made by the
L597@P19: City Council in 2021.

L1086@P34: To: Honorable Mayor and Members of the City Council
L1087@P34: From: Paul Buddenhagen, City Manager
L1088@P34: Re: Measure O Update
L1089@P34: This memo gives an overview of the City’s implementation thus far of Measure O, a
L1090@P34: 2018 ballot measure dedicated to increasing affordable housing.
L1091@P34: Measure O has thus far guided $109M toward an array of projects that will create at
L1092@P34: least 1,000 new affordable apartments and 44 shelter beds. This includes five
L1093@P34: completed projects, one project under construction, and a healthy pipeline of new
L1094@P34: construction projects in various stages of predevelopment and planning. Due to the
L1095@P34: robust Housing Trust Fund project pipeline, the City is on track to nearly double the
L1096@P34: number of restricted affordable units in its portfolio since 2018, largely thanks to the
L1097@P34: impact of Measure O. This powerful expansion of City investment in affordable
L1098@P34: housing will help low- and middle-income households in Berkeley.
L1099@P34: Building permanent affordable housing is complex, challenging and takes significant
L1100@P34: time. Affordable housing financing in California requires nonprofit developers to
L1101@P34: braid together funding from multiple sources. County, state, and federal sources
L1102@P34: usually require committed local funding – making the City’s investment a critical first
